mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 20-day return during the pre-rate-cut period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, reflecting stronger labor market momentum and investor optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 2-month moving average(PAYEMS) AND UNRATE < 2-month moving average(UNRATE)
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor cycle events, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 70% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2.5 standard deviations from its monthly mean for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals resilient supply-side momentum.
failure_condition: In 5 such events since 2000, the 60-day forward return is not positive in more than 40% of cases (binomial test p < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is more likely to be negative due to expectations of slower wage growth and reduced equity risk premia.
failure_condition: During 8 such low-inflation regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 20-day return during >2% inflation regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in residential housing starts (HOUST) by at least 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months coincides with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals economic expansion and demand recovery.
failure_condition: Across 12 such events since 2000, the 5-day forward return is not positive in more than 50% of cases (binomial test p < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) together predict a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting labor market tightness and investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 2-month moving average(PAYEMS) AND UNRATE < 2-month moving average(UNRATE) for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 8 such labor cycle tightness events, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of cases (binomial test p < 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly retail sales (GDPC1) by 5% or more for three consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals weakening consumer demand and economic softness.
failure_condition: During 6 such sales contraction regimes since 2000, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than during prior expansion regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positively correlated with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the same period, it suggests that easing labor market conditions amplify equity discounting, producing a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < UNRATE[3mo ago] AND CORR(GSPF_20d_return, UNRATE[-3mo]) > 0.3 over the last 3 months
regime_hint: Labor market easing detected via forward return correlation
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not positively correlated with UNRATE decline at the 10% significance level (F-test p > 0.1).
